title: Reading Drill — Comparing cameras at a nature hide — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Comparing cameras at a nature hide — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Millcross, work on moving birds being missed at the edge of the image had already produced a small collection of recording samples. The volunteer observer used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: the number of usable clips.

**B** The group kept a wider field of view for the new trial, which was planned to run for three weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that activity at different tides should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
